timing.basis: Two clock__curr_time readings; interval includes inspection, assessment and report composition, ending immediately before file serialization.

visible_export_metadata.interpretation: Consistent with 90 by 70 mm canvases after raster rounding. Previews are screen approximations. Raster content does not prove Arial or the authored 8 pt setting.

reasons: Both display endpoint years 1980 and 2024 and a clear upward annual series; endpoint values and delta can be read directly.
B's primary dots make the discrete annual observations more apparent at intended size, and its final-value leader explicitly associates 424.61 with the final observation.
B uses complete Annual mean CO2 and Uncertainty axis labels and a zero baseline for the uncertainty display.
Both captions distinguish supplied uncertainty from confidence intervals and within-year spread and disclose temporary Maunakea observations.
tradeoffs: A's connected lower trace makes constant uncertainty easy to see.
Neither primary-axis uncertainty encoding is resolvable at intended size; lower displays and captions are essential.

reader_questions.overall_change: answered by both images; captions state 338.76 to 424.61 ppm, delta 85.85 ppm, without source-value verification
reader_questions.supplied_uncertainty_retention_and_meani: value and stated meaning readable from lower plot plus caption in both; exact source fidelity unavailable

A.issue: Supplied ± uncertainty is unresolved on the concentration axis at intended size. The lower trace and explicit caption preserve its value and meaning, so this is a visibility limitation rather than demonstrated omission.
CO2 (ppm) and Unc. (ppm) require more caption support than B's full labels. The lower scale begins at 0.08 ppm, providing less absolute-size context than B's zero baseline.

B.issue: Primary-axis error bars are unresolved at intended size. The caption explicitly discloses this and lower dots display uncertainty independently.

tasks.blocking_failures: None established from the anonymous package.

reasons: Both identify logarithmic depth in kilometres and catalog magnitude. Shallow events around 10 km and deep events around 600 km can be compared.
B's hollow, distinct shapes better expose overlapping types, especially the purple mwr diamond near 7 km. A's pale filled marks are less distinct at intended size.

A provides a titled magnitude-type legend and caption explanations distinguishing body-wave magnitude from moment-magnitude estimates and their respective methods. B gives explicit type counts and documentation limits but does not expand the codes.
Both captions adequately describe a selected 131-event reviewed global January 2024 sample with magnitude and source restrictions and reject an all-earthquakes or completeness interpretation.
B's visual separation advantage and A's caption-level measurement explanation are material opposing advantages for the combined task; no clear overall winner is established.
tradeoffs: A supplies more scientific interpretation of the codes; the truth of those definitions cannot be verified within this package.
B is clearer for recognizing categories in the crowded scatter, but processing-method differences remain unavailable from B alone.

reader_questions.recognition_of_measurement_types: both encode four codes; A also explains measurement families in its caption, while B leaves processing meaning undocumented
reader_questions.catalog_sample_description: adequate in both captions as presented; source query, event counts and filtering claims are not independently audited
reader_questions.exact_overlap_multiplicity: unanswered by both images and explicitly acknowledged; not needed for requested comparison

A.issue: Pale filled orange squares and the tiny pink mwr triangle have weak prominence at intended size. Filled overlaps around 10 km reduce confidence in separating coincident types, including the rare mwb event.
Coincident event multiplicities cannot be recovered. The caption correctly acknowledges overlap and says transparency is not a calibrated count encoding; exact event counting is not requested.

B.issue: Hollow shapes improve separation, but outlines still superpose in the dense 10 km column. The single green mwb square is hard to isolate at intended size; coincident multiplicities remain unreadable.

The four original codes and nonuniform measurement are identified, but the codes' processing meanings are not explained. The explicit lack of processing-method documentation leaves that substantive comparison unanswered.

tasks.blocking_failures: None established for the basic depth and magnitude comparison. B has an explicit semantic limitation for explaining measurement methods.

shared_findings: Axes and units are readable in the intended-size previews.
No prohibited overall title, panel letter or footnote is established. Magnitude type in earthquake A is a permitted legend heading.
No material text clipping is visible. Explanatory prose is in the separate captions.
unavailable_facts: Exact correspondence to frozen source values, counts, uncertainty fields, omitted rows and transformations.
Truth of query/retrieval provenance, official uncertainty definition, and measurement-method definitions beyond caption claims.
Arial font identity and authored 8 pt setting in rasterized text.
Hidden export settings, other output formats, physical print reproduction and device-dependent display quality.
limits: Only the anonymous reading task, eight required images, four captions and metadata inside those PNGs were inspected.
96-dpi previews were treated as screen approximations, not delivered raster-resolution evidence.
Visual plausibility is not numerical validation, and supplied caption claims are not independent proof of source facts.
No source-value/export audit or external verification was performed.
